fail_to_pass._summary: 5 WindowITCase tests driving DataStream V2 window extension end-to-end via MiniCluster. The two-input tumbling-window method was removed by the source-symbol audit because its selected body directly instantiated the PR-added TwoInputNonBroadcastWindowStreamProcessFunction symbol, which is absent from the requirement doc.

pass_to_pass._summary: 50 untouched flink-clients selectors covering client options, packaged-program utilities, application entrypoint parsing, CLI dynamic properties, frontend info/list handling, and cluster-client service loading. They do not import or compile-depend on DataStream V2 window-extension classes, so they pass in both pre- and post-patch states.

triage.module_scope_rationale: flink-tests hosts WindowITCase. flink-clients is strict-§7 P2P.

mutant_set_revision.note: 2 §6-unreachable mutants removed: they flip WindowUtils.{delete,register}CleanupTimer from event-time to processing-time, but WindowUtils and the cleanup-timer time domain are internal (.impl.utils, 0 hits in requirement_docs) and the effect is not observable through any documented surface — the union suite's documented event-time window + allowed-lateness tests pass identically under golden and both mutants (confirmed by the full sweep). The remaining 41 mutants are all killed by union: the previously-surviving two-input/two-output mutants (020,023,024,025,026,042) are now killed by selecting the already-authored §6-clean testTwoInputTumblingContextBoundsAndBothRecordSides + testGlobalStreamTwoInputAndTwoOutputWindowRoutes; m002 + the sliding & lateness classes were killed earlier this pass.

triage.test_level_policy: Augmented F2P uses public DataStream V2 and WindowStrategy APIs through Flink's Maven/JUnit test harness: public strategy factories/getters, BuiltinFuncs.window wrappers, ExecutionEnvironment jobs, event-time watermarks, window contexts, and declared window state. Augmented P2P uses untouched flink-clients retry behavior and does not import window extension types.

org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.public_surface: WindowStrategy.sliding(Duration, Duration) two-argument default through BuiltinFuncs.window with event-time watermarks, OneInputWindowContext.getStartTime/getEndTime/getAllRecords.
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.rationale: Runs a keyed event-time sliding window built from the documented two-argument default factory and asserts event-time-only semantics: the slide-aligned [0, 5000) window fires with all five records, every window spans the configured size, and overlapping windows are spaced one slide interval apart. Under processing-time assignment the event watermarks never drive these windows, so no window starting at event-time 0 is observed.

requirement_sections: Proposed Changes > Define `WindowProcessFunction` > Store and access all records of a window
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.public_surface: WindowStrategy.sliding(Duration, Duration, TimeType, Duration) four-argument event-time factory through BuiltinFuncs.window, OneInputWindowContext.getStartTime/getEndTime/getAllRecords.
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.rationale: Exercises the documented four-argument sliding factory with EVENT_TIME and zero lateness, asserting the slide interval stays independent of the window size: the [0, 5000) window fires with all five records, windows span the configured size, and overlapping windows are one slide interval apart. A factory that propagates the size as the slide collapses the windows into non-overlapping spans and fails the gap assertion.

org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.public_surface: WindowStrategy.sliding(Duration, Duration) default and WindowStrategy.sliding(Duration, Duration, TimeType, Duration) explicit factories through BuiltinFuncs.window; OneInputWindowStreamProcessFunction.onLateRecord, OneInputWindowContext.getStartTime/getAllRecords; event-time watermarks.
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.rationale: Two event-time jobs assert the FLIP lateness contract for sliding windows. Job A uses the two-argument default (zero allowed lateness): a record arriving after its window has closed must reach onLateRecord, so a constructor that quietly substitutes the slide interval for lateness keeps the window open and reports no late record. Job B uses the four-argument factory with three seconds of allowed lateness: the same out-of-order record must stay inside its still-open [0, 5000) window, so a runtime that ignores the configured lateness (reads zero) expires the window early and reports the record as late instead.

org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.public_surface: WindowStrategy.tumbling(Duration) one-argument default through BuiltinFuncs.window; OneInputWindowStreamProcessFunction.onLateRecord; event-time watermarks.
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.rationale: The one-argument tumbling default must set allowed lateness to zero. A ts=4000 record in the single window [0, 5000) is late once the ts=5500 watermark closes the window, so it must reach onLateRecord exactly once. A constructor that quietly uses the window size as the default lateness keeps the window open and reports no late record.

requirement_sections: Proposed Changes > Define `WindowProcessFunction` > Store and access all records of a window
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.public_surface: WindowStrategy.tumbling(Duration, TimeType, Duration) explicit-lateness factory through BuiltinFuncs.window; OneInputWindowStreamProcessFunction.onLateRecord; OneInputWindowContext.getStartTime/getAllRecords; event-time watermarks.
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.rationale: A tumbling window configured with three seconds of allowed lateness keeps [0, 5000) open at watermark 5500, so the ts=4000 record stays in-window (window record count == 1) and is never late (late count == 0). A runtime that reads the configured tumbling lateness as zero, or a one-input BuiltinFuncs wrapper that forwards zero, expires the window early and reports the record as late instead.

org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.public_surface: WindowStrategy.tumbling(Duration) through BuiltinFuncs.window; OneInputWindowStreamProcessFunction.onLateRecord; event-time watermarks at the exact cleanup boundary.
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.rationale: With zero lateness the [0, 5000) window cleans up at maxTimestamp 4999. A second ts=4999 record arrives exactly at watermark 4999, so cleanupTime == watermark and timestamp == watermark. The inclusive (<=) window-late and element-late contract routes it to onLateRecord exactly once; a strict (<) boundary for either predicate instead accepts the record and emits no late record.

requirement_sections: Proposed Changes > Define `WindowProcessFunction` > Store and access all records of a window
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.public_surface: WindowStrategy.tumbling(Duration, TimeType, Duration) through the two-input BuiltinFuncs.window wrapper; TwoInputNonBroadcastWindowStreamProcessFunction.onLateRecord1/onLateRecord2/onTrigger; TwoInputWindowContext.getStartTime; event-time watermarks.
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.rationale: A two-input tumbling join with three seconds of allowed lateness keeps [0, 5000) open at watermark 5500 on both sides, so the ts=4000 records stay in-window (the window fires) and neither side reports a late record. A two-input BuiltinFuncs wrapper that forwards zero allowed lateness expires the window early and routes those records to onLateRecord1 / onLateRecord2.
